title: Review 2 untracked source file(s) — keep, ignore, or delete
perceive: A fleet-wide git health sweep on 2026-07-31 found 2 untracked SOURCE file(s) in this spoke — real code, not harness state.

mywheel committed every generated harness record across the fleet, but deliberately did NOT touch project source: committing unreviewed code blind is laundering, and only this spoke knows whether these files are wanted.
Untracked source is the last thing standing between this spoke and a clean git state. It is also a loss risk — nothing here exists anywhere but this machine.
execute: Review this list WITH THE OPERATOR in the next session — that is the point of routing it here rather than deciding it centrally.
For each file decide one of three: COMMIT (wanted work), IGNORE (add to .gitignore with a reason), or DELETE (scratch that was never meant to live).
Do not bulk-commit to clear the list. A file nobody can account for is the one worth asking about.
Where a whole directory is generated output, add the directory to .gitignore rather than listing files.
verify: the command above returns nothing, OR every remaining entry is explained in this lug's completion note
acceptance_criteria: Every listed file is committed, ignored-with-a-reason, or deleted — none left unexplained.
The decision was made with the operator present, not inferred.
This spoke reports GREEN on the next fleet git-health run, or states why not.

_improvement_lenses.skeptic: The cheap close is `git add -A`, which buries whatever should not have been committed inside a large diff nobody reads. The lug exists precisely because the central sweep refused to do that.
_improvement_lenses.architect: Untracked source is the one category a fleet-level tool cannot judge — it needs the project's own context, which is why it routes to the spoke rather than being decided in the hub.
_improvement_lenses.naive_reader: There are files here that were never saved to the repo. Someone should say whether they matter before they are lost or committed by accident.
